newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-NZ batsmen bamboozled by English spinners.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NZ batsmen bamboozled by English spinners.

text.p: CHRISTCHURCH, Feb 17 - The lessons of a week ago weren't absorbed by New Zealand's batsmen as they slumped during a critical session in the third and final cricket test against England here yesterday.

During the heavy second-test loss to England at the Basin Reserve in Wellington last week, New Zealand's batsmen contributed to their downfall with a negative attitude late on the fourth day against spinners Robert Croft and Phil Tufnell.

Recent history repeated itself at Lancaster Park yesterday as New Zealand, armed with a precious 118-run first-innings lead after bowling England out for 228, slumped to 95 for six wickets in their second innings.
Croft and Tufnell bowled unchanged for 32 overs and shared four wickets for 42 runs.
Offspinner Croft ended the day with two for 25 from 20 overs while left-arm spinner Tufnell took two for 24 from 18 overs.

Only opener Bryan Young seemed able to compete on a level footing with the two English spinners. He made a composed 49 in 165 minutes before being controversially caught at silly mid off by Nick Knight off Tufnell.

Adam Parore, who made a determined 59 in New Zealand's first innings, scratched around for 55 balls over eight; captain Stephen Fleming got 11 in 34 balls while Nathan Astle could manage only five in 36 balls.
The first 22 overs produced just 42 runs as England fought to get themselves back into a test New Zealand need to win to level the three-match series.
"We have to take on a more attacking role," New Zealand coach Steve Rixon said last night.
"We didn't respond too well to the style of bowling from Tufnell.
"He was bowling into the footmarks and it was obviously a little awkward -- and there was a bit of inexperience as well."
Four of the six New Zealand wickets yesterday fell to catches close to the wicket as the Kiwis lost their way.
Knight pouched catches off Fleming, Young and Simon Doull in close on the offside while Nasser Hussain caught Astle at slip off Croft in an identical end to the New Zealanders' first innings.
In the drawn first test at Auckland, Tufnell picked up three for 53 from 40 overs in New Zealand's second innings.
At Wellington, Croft took three for 19 from 20 overs and Tufnell one for 29 from 23 overs as they tied the New Zealand batsmen in knots in the second innings.
Croft grabbed five for 95 in the first innings of the Christchurch test in 39.1 overs for his best test figures and the pair shared 15 wickets in the two tests in Zimbabwe en route to New Zealand.
"It's a delight being captain of a side with two quality spinners," England captain Mike Atherton said last night.
"It's been one of the most enjoyable things this winter.
"Croft and Tufnell give a lot of options and variety. They constantly ask questions of the batsmen.
"Croft always bowls a challenging line; Tufnell needs the pitch to hold for him, then his change of pace comes into it."
Atherton believed the ability of the two to keep the heat on the New Zealand batsmen during the last two tests has been a crucial aspect in England's success.
"The pressure is always on the batsmen. You build up the pressure because they're two spinners who don't bowl a lot of bad balls.
"You can sense it building up. It built up at Wellington and you could feel it today, and with the pressure of the close fielders it's not an easy game."
